text: Late shipment SOP. If dwell exceeds the carrier transit commitment and quantity observed still matches quantity expected, contact the carrier desk, request a revised ETA, and move the next production or store wave to safety stock before rebooking. Do not treat a late but complete trailer as a shortage.

Stockout SOP. When observed quantity is near zero against a live pick wave, freeze new allocations for that SKU, pull from the designated safety location, and expedite the inbound ASN that covers the deficit. Escalate if the consuming site is a hospital pharmacy or a JIT line.

Overstock SOP. If observed quantity is materially above expected, stop further receipts for the SKU, redirect the excess to overflow or a returns lane, and ask planning to cut the next purchase order. Do not quarantine product only because it is surplus.

Quality reject SOP. Quarantine the failed lot, block the SKU location in the WMS, and notify the supplier quality contact with the inspection result. Do not put the lot away or allocate it to a customer order.

Customs hold SOP. When observed quantity is zero and the broker has no release time, send the commercial invoice and packing list again, ask the broker for the hold reason code, and switch the wave to an already-cleared substitute if one exists.

Carrier no-show SOP. If the booked truck did not collect, tender the load to the backup carrier on the lane card and notify the receiving site of the new ETA. Record the miss against the carrier scorecard.

Demand spike SOP. When same-day orders jump above the trailing baseline and on-hand cannot cover them, release safety stock, cap promotional allocations, and raise an expedite on the next firm receipt. Recalculate the allocation before promising customers.

Forecast miss SOP. If actual demand or receipts diverge from the locked forecast, update the short-horizon forecast, rebalance inventory to the sites that are short, and leave a note for the demand planner. Do not scrap product solely because the forecast was wrong.

Cold-chain excursion SOP. A labelled 2 to 8 Celsius product with a logger above 8 Celsius stays in quarantine. Do not put it away. Open a quality deviation, keep the logger file with the lot, and wait for quality disposition before any customer allocation.

Duplicate ASN SOP. If two advance ship notices reference one handling unit, receive against a single ASN, cancel or merge the duplicate in the WMS, and confirm the physical carton count before putaway so inventory is not doubled.

Lead-time drift SOP. When the 30-day on-time rate is weak and dwell is beyond the master-data lead time, update the planning lead time, review safety stock, and ask the supplier for a recovery calendar. Do not keep promising the old lead time.

Mispick SOP. Stop the outbound trailer if it has not departed, recount the order line, and ship the missing units from the correct location. File a warehouse quality event so the location can be cycle-counted.

Port congestion SOP. If the container has no berth and observed quantity at the DC is zero, identify a substitute SKU already on hand, inform the customer of the revised date, and avoid booking a pickup that the terminal cannot release.

MOQ breach SOP. If the purchase order is below the supplier minimum, either raise the quantity to the minimum and store the extra, or switch to a distributor that can break the pack. Do not leave the order open if the supplier has already rejected it.

Damage on receipt SOP. Photograph the cartons, move damaged units to the claims location, and file the carrier or supplier claim before putaway. Only the undamaged remainder may be received into available stock.
